sanskrit: skandham āropya bhadraṃ te madhye 'smākaṃ vihāyasā gaccha nīcikayā gatyā yathā caināṃ na pīḍayeḥ
english: Having placed her on your shoulder, blessings be upon you — fly through the sky in our midst, but move gently so that you do not cause her pain.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaca uvāca dharmarājaṃ ca dhaumyaṃ ca rājaputrīṃ yamau tathā eko 'py aham alaṃ voḍhuṃ kim utādya sahāyavān
english: Ghaṭotkaca said: Even alone I am capable of carrying the king of dharma, Dhaumya, the princess, and the twin brothers — how much more so now, when I have helpers with me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tataḥ kṛṣṇām uvāha sa ghaṭotkacaḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ madhyago vīraḥ pāṇḍavān api cāpare
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Ghaṭotkaca then carried Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) upon his back; that hero moved among the Pāṇḍavas, while the other rakshasas carried the Pāṇḍavas themselves.

sanskrit: lomaśaḥ siddhamārgeṇa jagāmānupamadyutiḥ svenaivātmaprabhāvena dvitīya iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Lomaśa, of incomparable brilliance, traveled by the path of the siddhas, shining by his own inner power, like a second sun.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāṃś cāpi tān sarvān samupādāya rākṣasāḥ niyogād rākṣasendrasya jagmur bhīmaparākramāḥ
english: The rakshasas of fearsome valor took up all those brahmins as well and, by order of the lord of rakshasas, set forth.

sanskrit: evaṃ suramaṇīyāni vanāny upavanāni ca ālokayantas te jagmur viśālāṃ badarīṃ prati
english: Thus beholding the divinely beautiful forests and groves, they journeyed on toward the great Badarī.

sanskrit: te tv āśugatibhir vīrā rākṣasais tair mahābalaiḥ uhyamānā yayuḥ śīghraṃ mahad adhvānam alpavat
english: Borne by those swift-moving, mightily powerful rakshasas, the heroes traveled swiftly; the long road seemed as nothing.

sanskrit: deśān mlecchagaṇākīrṇān nānāratnākarāyutān dadṛśur giripādāṃś ca nānādhātusamācitān
english: They saw lands thronging with barbarian peoples, rich with mines of many jewels, and mountain foothills streaked with various minerals.

sanskrit: vidyādharagaṇākīrṇān yutān vānarakiṃnaraiḥ tathā kiṃpuruṣaiś caiva gandharvaiś ca samantataḥ
english: They saw regions crowded with hosts of vidyadharas, filled with apes and kinnaras, as well as kimpurushas and gandharvas on every side.

sanskrit: nadījālasamākīrṇān nānāpakṣirutākulān nānāvidhair mṛgair juṣṭān vānaraiś copaśobhitān
english: They saw lands laced with networks of rivers, filled with the calls of many birds, frequented by all manner of deer, and adorned with troops of monkeys.

sanskrit: te vyatītya bahūn deśān uttarāṃś ca kurūn api dadṛśur vividhāścaryaṃ kailāsaṃ parvatottamam
english: Having passed through many lands and even the northern Kurus, they beheld the wondrous and extraordinary Kailāsa, the greatest of mountains.

sanskrit: tasyābhyāśe tu dadṛśur naranārāyaṇāśramam upetaṃ pādapair divyaiḥ sadāpuṣpaphalopagaiḥ
english: Near that mountain they saw the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, adorned with divine trees ever laden with flowers and fruits.

sanskrit: dadṛśus tāṃ ca badarīṃ vṛttaskandhāṃ manoramām snigdhām aviralacchāyāṃ śriyā paramayā yutām
english: They saw that jujube tree (badari), lovely with its rounded trunk, glossy, casting a dense unbroken shade, endowed with surpassing beauty.

sanskrit: patraiḥ snigdhair aviralair upetāṃ mṛdubhiḥ śubhām viśālaśākhāṃ vistīrṇām atidyutisamanvitām
english: It was covered with glossy, dense, soft, and auspicious leaves; its branches were wide and spreading, endowed with extraordinary radiance.

sanskrit: phalair upacitair divyair ācitāṃ svādubhir bhṛśam madhusravaiḥ sadā divyāṃ maharṣigaṇasevitām madapramuditair nityaṃ nānādvijagaṇair yutām
english: It was laden with divine fruits, heavily covered with sweet honey-dripping berries — that divine tree, always frequented by bands of great sages and by flocks of various birds perpetually joyful and enraptured.

sanskrit: adaṃśamaśake deśe bahumūlaphalodake nīlaśādvalasaṃchanne devagandharvasevite
english: In a place free of gnats and mosquitoes, abounding in roots and fruits and water, covered with blue-green grass, and visited by gods and gandharvas —

sanskrit: susamīkṛtabhūbhāge svabhāvavihite śubhe jātāṃ himamṛdusparśe deśe 'pahatakaṇṭake
english: — in a region of ground naturally well-leveled and auspicious, where the air was cool and soft as dew, in a place clear of thorns —

sanskrit: tām upetya mahātmānaḥ saha tair brāhmaṇarṣabhaiḥ avaterus tataḥ sarve rākṣasaskandhataḥ śanaiḥ
english: — arriving at that place, the great-souled ones together with those foremost brahmins all descended gently from the shoulders of the rakshasas.

sanskrit: tatas tam āśramaṃ puṇyaṃ naranārāyaṇāśritam dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan sahitā dvijapuṃgavaiḥ
english: Then, O king, the Pāṇḍavas together with the foremost twice-born sages beheld that sacred hermitage, the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tamasā rahitaṃ puṇyam anāmṛṣṭaṃ raveḥ karaiḥ kṣuttṛṭśītoṣṇadoṣaiś ca varjitaṃ śokanāśanam
english: It was free of darkness, holy, untouched by the rays of the sun, free from the afflictions of hunger, thirst, cold, and heat — a destroyer of grief.

sanskrit: maharṣigaṇasaṃbādhaṃ brāhmyā lakṣmyā samanvitam duṣpraveśaṃ mahārāja narair dharmabahiṣkṛtaiḥ
english: It was thronged with hosts of great sages and endowed with the splendor of brahman; inaccessible, O great king, to men who have forsaken dharma.

sanskrit: balihomārcitaṃ divyaṃ susaṃmṛṣṭānulepanam divyapuṣpopahāraiś ca sarvato 'bhivirājitam
english: It was divine, honored with offerings and ritual fire, its surfaces well-swept and anointed, radiant on all sides with offerings of divine flowers.

sanskrit: viśālair agniśaraṇaiḥ srugbhāṇḍair ācitaṃ śubhaiḥ mahadbhis toyakalaśaiḥ kaṭhinaiś copaśobhitam śaraṇyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam
english: It was filled with spacious fire-halls and auspicious ritual vessels, adorned with large water-pots and wooden ladles; it was a refuge for all beings and resonant with the chanting of the Veda.

sanskrit: divyam āśrayaṇīyaṃ tam āśramaṃ śramanāśanam śriyā yutam anirdeśyaṃ devacaryopaśobhitam
english: That divine hermitage, worthy of taking refuge in, a destroyer of weariness, endowed with beauty beyond description, resplendent with the practices of the gods.

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanair dāntaiś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraiḥ sūryavaiśvānarasamais tapasā bhāvitātmabhiḥ
english: It was filled with self-controlled ones who lived on fruits and roots, clad in bark-cloth and black deerskins, whose selves were refined by austerities equal to the sun and sacred fire —

sanskrit: maharṣibhir mokṣaparair yatibhir niyatendriyaiḥ brahmabhūtair mahābhāgair upetaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ
english: — with great sages intent on liberation, ascetics whose senses were restrained, who had become Brahman, of great fortune, and who were expounders of brahman.

sanskrit: so 'bhyagacchan mahātejās tān ṛṣīn niyataḥ śuciḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito dhīmān dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The wise Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, of great splendor, disciplined and pure, together with his brothers, went forward to meet those sages.

sanskrit: divyajñānopapannās te dṛṣṭvā prāptaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram abhyagacchanta suprītāḥ sarva eva maharṣayaḥ āśīrvādān prayuñjānāḥ svādhyāyaniratā bhṛśam
english: Endowed with divine knowledge, seeing that Yudhiṣṭhira had arrived, all the great sages came forward with great delight, uttering blessings upon him, devoted as they were to Vedic recitation.

sanskrit: prītās te tasya satkāraṃ vidhinā pāvakopamāḥ upājahruś ca salilaṃ puṣpamūlaphalaṃ śuci
english: Delighted, those sages who were like fire performed for him proper honor according to rite, and brought water, flowers, roots, and pure fruits.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ prītyātha satkāram upanītaṃ maharṣibhiḥ prayataḥ pratigṛhyātha dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, received with devotion the honor thus rendered to him by the great sages with love.

sanskrit: taṃ śakrasadanaprakhyaṃ divyagandhaṃ manoramam prītaḥ svargopamaṃ puṇyaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ saha kṛṣṇayā
english: That hermitage resembling the abode of Śakra, fragrant with divine scents, lovely, equal to heaven in its holiness — the Pāṇḍava, full of joy, together with Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) —

sanskrit: viveśa śobhayā yuktaṃ bhrātṛbhiś ca sahānagha brāhmaṇair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ ca sahācyutaḥ
english: — entered it, endowed with beauty, together with his brothers, O sinless one, and together with brahmins versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, accompanied by the unfailing one.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyat sa dharmātmā devadevarṣipūjitam naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ bhāgīrathyopaśobhitam
english: There that dharma-souled one saw the sacred seat of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, honored by gods and divine sages, adorned by the Bhāgīrathī.

sanskrit: madhusravaphalāṃ divyāṃ maharṣigaṇasevitām tām upetya mahātmānas te 'vasan brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
english: Having reached that divine badari tree, dripping with honey and fruit, frequented by bands of great sages, the great-souled ones dwelt there together with the brahmins.

sanskrit: ālokayanto mainākaṃ nānādvijagaṇāyutam hiraṇyaśikharaṃ caiva tac ca bindusaraḥ śivam
english: They beheld mount Maināka filled with many flocks of birds, and the golden-peaked mountain, and that auspicious lake Bindusaras.

sanskrit: bhāgīrathīṃ sutīrthāṃ ca śītāmalajalāṃ śivām maṇipravālaprastārāṃ pādapair upaśobhitām
english: They beheld the Bhāgīrathī with its excellent fords, its cool and pure waters, auspicious, with banks strewn with gems and coral, adorned with trees.

sanskrit: divyapuṣpasamākīrṇāṃ manasaḥ prītivardhanīm vīkṣamāṇā mahātmāno vijahrus tatra pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Beholding it, strewn with divine flowers and gladdening the mind, the great-souled Pāṇḍavas took their delight there.

sanskrit: tatra devān pitṝṃś caiva tarpayantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitā vīrā nyavasan puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: There those foremost of men, those heroes, dwelling with the brahmins, repeatedly offered satisfaction to the gods and the ancestors.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāyās tatra paśyantaḥ krīḍitāny amaraprabhāḥ vicitrāṇi naravyāghrā remire tatra pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Watching the various delightful pastimes of Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) there, those tiger-like men, the Pāṇḍavas, shining like immortals, rejoiced in that place.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatra te puruṣavyāghrāḥ paramaṃ śaucam āsthitāḥ ṣaḍrātram avasan vīrā dhanaṃjayadidṛkṣayā tasmin viharamāṇāś ca ramamāṇāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There those tiger-like men, those heroes, observing the strictest purity and longing to see Dhanañjaya, the Pāṇḍavas dwelt for six nights, roaming and taking pleasure in that place.

sanskrit: manojñe kānanavare sarvabhūtamanorame pādapaiḥ puṣpavikacaiḥ phalabhārāvanāmitaiḥ
english: In that most excellent and delightful forest, pleasing to all creatures, with trees in full bloom and bending under the weight of their fruits —

sanskrit: śobhitaṃ sarvatoramyaiḥ puṃskokilakulākulaiḥ snigdhapatrair aviralaiḥ śītacchāyair manoramaiḥ
english: — adorned on every side by pleasing trees, crowded with flocks of male kokilas, with glossy dense leaves casting cool and lovely shade —

sanskrit: sarāṃsi ca vicitrāṇi prasannasalilāni ca kamalaiḥ sotpalais tatra bhrājamānāni sarvaśaḥ paśyantaś cārurūpāṇi remire tatra pāṇḍavāḥ
english: — and various lakes with clear waters gleaming on all sides with lotuses and blue water-lilies — beholding all these lovely forms, the Pāṇḍavas took their delight in that place.

sanskrit: puṇyagandhaḥ sukhasparśo vavau tatra samīraṇaḥ hlādayan pāṇḍavān sarvān sakṛṣṇān sadvijarṣabhān
english: There blew a breeze of holy fragrance and pleasant touch, gladdening all the Pāṇḍavas together with Kṛṣṇa and the foremost twice-born sages.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvottaro vāyuḥ pavamāno yadṛcchayā sahasrapatram arkābhaṃ divyaṃ padmam udāvahat
english: Then the wind blowing from the northeast carried by chance a divine lotus, brilliant as the sun, with a thousand petals.

sanskrit: tad apaśyata pāñcālī divyagandhaṃ manoramam anilenāhṛtaṃ bhūmau patitaṃ jalajaṃ śuci
english: The princess of Pāñcāla saw it — divinely fragrant, lovely, borne by the wind and fallen upon the ground, that pure water-born flower.

sanskrit: tac chubhā śubham āsādya saugandhikam anuttamam atīva muditā rājan bhīmasenam athābravīt
english: That auspicious one, having obtained that unrivaled saugandhika lotus, was exceedingly delighted, O king, and then spoke to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: paśya divyaṃ suruciraṃ bhīma puṣpam anuttamam gandhasaṃsthānasaṃpannaṃ manaso mama nandanam
english: "Look, Bhīma, at this divine, exceedingly beautiful, unrivaled flower, perfect in fragrance and form — it is a delight to my heart."

sanskrit: etat tu dharmarājāya pradāsyāmi paraṃtapa harer idaṃ me kāmāya kāmyake punar āśrame
english: "I shall give this to the king of dharma, O scorcher of foes; it is my wish to have more of these when we return to the Kāmyaka forest."

sanskrit: yadi te 'haṃ priyā pārtha bahūnīmāny upāhara tāny ahaṃ netum icchāmi kāmyakaṃ punar āśramam
english: "If I am dear to you, O Pārtha, bring many of these flowers — I wish to take them back to the Kāmyaka hermitage."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu pāñcālī bhīmasenam aninditā jagāma dharmarājāya puṣpam ādāya tat tadā
english: Having spoken thus to Bhīmasena, the blameless princess of Pāñcāla took the flower and went to the king of dharma.

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ tu vijñāya mahiṣyāḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ priyāyāḥ priyakāmaḥ sa bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: Understanding the intention of his queen, that bull among men, Bhīma of fearsome valor, desirous of pleasing his beloved —

sanskrit: vātaṃ tam evābhimukho yatas tat puṣpam āgatam ājihīrṣur jagāmāśu sa puṣpāṇy aparāṇy api
english: — turned himself in the very direction of the wind from which that flower had come, intent on fetching it, and set off swiftly to get more flowers as well.

sanskrit: rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ dhanur gṛhya śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān mṛgarāḍ iva saṃkruddhaḥ prabhinna iva kuñjaraḥ
english: Taking up his bow with its golden back and arrows like venomous serpents, like a lion enraged, like an elephant in rut —

sanskrit: draupadyāḥ priyam anvicchan svabāhubalam āśritaḥ vyapetabhayasaṃmohaḥ śailam abhyapatad balī
english: — seeking to please Draupadī, relying on the strength of his own arms, free from fear and confusion, the mighty one rushed up the mountain.

sanskrit: sa taṃ drumalatāgulmacchannaṃ nīlaśilātalam giriṃ cacārāriharaḥ kiṃnarācaritaṃ śubham
english: He who destroys enemies roamed over that mountain, beautiful, frequented by kinnaras, with its floor of dark rock covered with trees, creepers, and thickets.

sanskrit: nānāvarṇadharaiś citraṃ dhātudrumamṛgāṇḍajaiḥ sarvabhūṣaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ bhūmer bhujam ivocchritam
english: The mountain was variegated with minerals, trees, animals, and birds of many colors, filled with every ornament, raised up like an arm of the earth.

sanskrit: sarvarturamaṇīyeṣu gandhamādanasānuṣu saktacakṣur abhiprāyaṃ hṛdayenānucintayan
english: On the peaks of Gandhamādana, lovely in every season, his eyes absorbed in the scenery, he reflected in his heart upon his purpose —

sanskrit: puṃskokilaninādeṣu ṣaṭpadābhiruteṣu ca baddhaśrotramanaścakṣur jagāmāmitavikramaḥ
english: — with his ears, mind, and eyes riveted by the songs of male kokilas and the hum of bees, that one of boundless valor moved forward.

sanskrit: jighramāṇo mahātejāḥ sarvartukusumodbhavam gandham uddāmam uddāmo vane matta iva dvipaḥ
english: Inhaling the overpowering fragrance arising from the blossoms of every season, that one of great splendor moved freely through the forest like a maddened elephant.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇaśramaḥ pitrā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ pituḥ saṃsparśaśītena gandhamādanavāyunā
english: His fatigue carried away by his father, his body hair thrilling with joy, touched by the cool breeze of Gandhamādana — the breeze that was his father's caress —

sanskrit: sa yakṣagandharvasurabrahmarṣigaṇasevitam viloḍayām āsa tadā puṣpahetor ariṃdamaḥ
english: — that tamer of enemies churned through the forest — haunted by bands of yakshas, gandharvas, suras, and brahmarshis — in search of the flowers.

sanskrit: viṣamacchedaracitair anuliptam ivāṅgulaiḥ vimalair dhātuvicchedaiḥ kāñcanāñjanarājataiḥ
english: The mountain appeared smeared as if by fingers tracing uneven lines, its strata of brilliant minerals — golden, dark, and silver — creating varied streaks across its face.

sanskrit: sapakṣam iva nṛtyantaṃ pārśvalagnaiḥ payodharaiḥ muktāhārair iva citaṃ cyutaiḥ prasravaṇodakaiḥ
english: The mountain seemed to dance with wings, with clouds clinging to its flanks; it seemed adorned with pearl necklaces, with cascades of water falling from its springs.

sanskrit: abhirāmanadīkuñjanirjharodarakandaram apsaronūpuraravaiḥ pranṛttabahubarhiṇam
english: Its interior was filled with delightful river-groves and gorges with cascades; many peacocks danced within to the sound of the anklets of apsaras.

sanskrit: digvāraṇaviṣāṇāgrair ghṛṣṭopalaśilātalam srastāṃśukam ivākṣobhyair nimnagāniḥsṛtair jalaiḥ
english: Its rocky surface was polished by the tusks of the elephants of the quarters; the waters flowing out of its streams made it appear as if its garment had slipped.

sanskrit: saśaṣpakavalaiḥ svasthair adūraparivartibhiḥ bhayasyājñaiś ca hariṇaiḥ kautūhalanirīkṣitaḥ
english: Bhīma was observed with curiosity by deer at ease, grazing on fresh shoots, moving about nearby, ignorant of fear.

sanskrit: cālayann ūruvegena latājālāny anekaśaḥ ākrīḍamānaḥ kaunteyaḥ śrīmān vāyusuto yayau
english: Shaking many networks of creepers with the speed of his thighs, playing as he went, the glorious son of Kuntī, child of the Wind, moved on.

sanskrit: priyāmanorathaṃ kartum udyataś cārulocanaḥ prāṃśuḥ kanakatālābhaḥ siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā
english: Intent on fulfilling the desire of his beloved, beautiful-eyed, tall, golden as a palm tree, with the build of a lion, youthful —

sanskrit: mattavāraṇavikrānto mattavāraṇavegavān mattavāraṇatāmrākṣo mattavāraṇavāraṇaḥ
english: — with the stride of a maddened elephant, the speed of a maddened elephant, eyes red as a maddened elephant, and the unstoppability of a maddened elephant —

sanskrit: priyapārśvopaviṣṭābhir vyāvṛttābhir viceṣṭitaiḥ yakṣagandharvayoṣābhir adṛśyābhir nirīkṣitaḥ
english: — he was observed by invisible yaksha and gandharva women who sat nearby, turning to look at him and making gestures of admiration.

sanskrit: navāvatāraṃ rūpasya vikrīṇann iva pāṇḍavaḥ cacāra ramaṇīyeṣu gandhamādanasānuṣu
english: As though displaying a freshly descended form of beauty, the Pāṇḍava roamed the delightful peaks of Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: saṃsmaran vividhān kleśān duryodhanakṛtān bahūn draupadyā vanavāsinyāḥ priyaṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ
english: Remembering the many and varied hardships inflicted by Duryodhana, he was intent on doing what was dear to Draupadī, who was dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: so 'cintayad gate svargam arjune mayi cāgate puṣpahetoḥ kathaṃ nv āryaḥ kariṣyati yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: He thought: "With Arjuna gone to heaven and myself gone in search of flowers, how will the noble Yudhiṣṭhira manage?"

sanskrit: snehān naravaro nūnam aviśvāsād vanasya ca nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca na mokṣyati yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Out of affection, and out of distrust of the forest, that best of men Yudhiṣṭhira will surely not release Nakula and Sahadeva."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu kusumāvāptiḥ syāc chīghram iti cintayan pratasthe naraśārdūlaḥ pakṣirāḍ iva vegitaḥ
english: Thinking, "How shall I obtain the flowers quickly?" that tiger among men set off with the speed of the king of birds.

sanskrit: kampayan medinīṃ padbhyāṃ nirghāta iva parvasu trāsayan gajayūthāni vātaraṃhā vṛkodaraḥ
english: Making the earth tremble with his feet like a thunderclap upon a mountain, frightening herds of elephants, wolf-bellied Bhīma moved swift as the wind.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghragaṇāṃś caiva mardamāno mahābalaḥ unmūlayan mahāvṛkṣān pothayaṃś corasā balī
english: Crushing packs of lions and tigers, uprooting great trees and smashing them against his chest, the immensely strong and mighty one pressed on.

sanskrit: latāvallīś ca vegena vikarṣan pāṇḍunandanaḥ upary upari śailāgram ārurukṣur iva dvipaḥ vinardamāno 'tibhṛśaṃ savidyud iva toyadaḥ
english: Tearing away creepers and vines with great force, the son of Pāṇḍu, roaring mightily like a thundercloud attended by lightning, strode upward to the summit of the mountain like an elephant.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena ghoreṇa dhanurghoṣeṇa cābhibho trastāni mṛgayūthāni samantād vipradudruvuḥ
english: At his terrible roar and the twang of his bow, O mighty one, herds of deer fled in terror on every side.
